standardCustomAssumptions: Scenario amounts are user-defined assumptions. Refreshing statistics does not replace them.
standardEstimatedAssumptions: Scenario amounts are calculated estimates from the reported statistics below, rather than a personal financial assessment.
standardCanadaMethod: Canada: one single worker without children earning 100% of the average wage, with OECD modeled take-home income using Ontario taxes. This is a mean wage, not a median wage. Spending uses Statistics Canada one-person households across ages and housing tenures; these are not the same population as employed adults. Essential costs group shelter, groceries and household operations (including communications). All other consumption, including transport and health, is retained in everyday spending. Total consumption includes shelter expenditures across owners and renters, so it is not a market rent quote or a precise cash budget. 2023 spending is adjusted to 2025 prices using the annual all-items CPI ratio. This is an estimate; it does not predict future inflation or your individual circumstances.
standardCanadaSources:
OECD Taxing Wages 2026, Canada (2025 model): https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/taxing-wages-2026_3a5169ef-en/full-report/canada_4b146e35.html
Statistics Canada tables 11-10-0224-01 and 18-10-0005-01:
https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1110022401
https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000501
Bank of Canada indicative daily average exchange rates: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/exchange/
standardCalculation: Monthly conversions use 365.25 days per year and 12 months per year. Saving capacity is take-home income minus essential costs and everyday spending. All positive capacity is assigned to this single hypothetical goal; other personal plans are not included. The goal uses the selected plan’s remaining amount, including its existing allocation calculation. Prices, income and the displayed exchange rate remain constant. Money is rounded to hundredths and completion days are rounded up. Completion dates use your selected calendar in DD/MM/YYYY. No financial history is changed and expected income is not treated as received income.
standardExchangeSource: Bank of Canada · indicative daily average · 1 {currency} = {rate} CAD · reference {date} (Gregorian). This is not a transaction quote.
standardCustomizeHint: Optional scenario only. Enter take-home income, essential costs and everyday spending as separate amounts without counting any cost twice. These assumptions are saved locally and included in backups. They never replace your recorded financial data.
standardCustomRateHint: Optional conversion assumption, up to 12 decimals. Supply a rate matching your intended exchange basis. Traditional toman means 10 Iranian rials; an official rate may differ substantially from the consumer market rate.
standardIranLimitations: Iran uses reported income and spending for an urban household, not an individual salary. Income includes business, transfers and non-cash income; the resulting saving capacity is a household survey scenario, not guaranteed cash. This basis differs from the single-worker OECD scenarios. Adjust the assumptions for an individual comparison.
standardIranSource: Statistical Centre of Iran, urban Household Income and Expenditure Survey 1404: https://amar.org.ir/news/id/19255. Values in thousand rials are multiplied by 100 to get traditional toman. Currency conversion uses the TGJU free-market USD quote and Bank of Canada cross-rates. Historical survey values are held constant.
standardReviewRequired: The provider returned data outside the reviewed periods, units or quality requirements. Existing cached data have been kept. This source mapping needs review before the new data can be used.
standardRequiredSaving: Monthly saving needed by target date
standardDeadlineMethod: Required saving = remaining goal ÷ time until target date. Required take-home income = living costs + required saving. Completion uses benchmark income minus living costs, with no interest, future inflation or wage growth. This is a scenario, not a promise. Each comparison considers this goal independently; registered savings are allocated once by priority.
standardInternationalMethod: Income: OECD modeled net earnings for a single worker without children at the average wage. Living costs: World Bank annual household consumption divided by population, a national per-person benchmark, not a city rent quote. Income and spending may refer to different years (up to two years apart).
